title: Avert a missed payroll
summary: Payroll is a hard deadline: providers debit funds days before payday, and wages for hours worked are owed in full. An employer who misses the FLSA minimum-wage or overtime floor owes the unpaid wages plus an equal amount as liquidated damages (law rule us-fed.flsa-unpaid-wages-liability), state wage statutes add penalties of their own, and if anyone is let go the final-pay clocks run from the termination itself (in California, immediately: law rule us-ca.final-wages-timing). So face the number first: true cash against the payroll funding deadline. Then work the options in order: written deferral consents only where they are lawful at all (deferrals cannot dip below the statutory floors, law rule us-fed.flsa-minimum-wage-overtime), an officer loan papered as a real note, an insider bridge on SAFEs, and the emergency cost plan. Decide the fork while payroll can still be paid: bridge, cut to default-alive, or an orderly wind-down that pays final wages on time. Tell the board before payday and the team before the rumor. Educational guidance, not legal advice; the exposure sits in the wage statutes, so verify them at the primary source.

parts.title: Face the number: true cash against the payroll funding deadline, which lands days before payday when the provider debits

execution.rationale: Recompute cash, burn, and the funding-debit date from the supplied bank balances, books, and payroll calendar; the output is the honest gap, not a decision.

parts.title: Size the wage exposure before choosing a path: pay for hours worked is owed in full, and missing it compounds
parts.guidance: An employer who violates the FLSA minimum-wage or overtime provisions owes the unpaid wages and an additional equal amount as liquidated damages (law rule us-fed.flsa-unpaid-wages-liability). State wage statutes add penalties on top, and if anyone is terminated the final-pay clocks run from the termination itself (law rule us-ca.final-wages-timing in California).

geoResolutions.label: Exposure runs through the FLSA (unpaid wages plus equal liquidated damages, law rule us-fed.flsa-unpaid-wages-liability) and the state wage statutes, with final-pay clocks like California's (law rule us-ca.final-wages-timing)

execution.rationale: Tally the wages owed this run from the payroll register and mark the statutory floors the cited rules state; counsel reads the result.

parts.title: Ask for written deferral consents only where they are lawful: consent does not erase the statutory floors for hours worked
parts.guidance: A deferral below the FLSA minimum wage or overtime floor stays a violation with or without consent, and exempt employees have a salary basis that a partial payment can break (law rule us-fed.flsa-minimum-wage-overtime). Deferrals that survive that screen get documented in writing, per person, with the repayment date.

execution.rationale: The founder asks each affected person directly and employment counsel screens which deferrals are lawful before any are accepted.

parts.title: Fund the gap if the math works: an officer loan papered as a real note, or an insider bridge on SAFEs

execution.rationale: The founder raises the bridge or lends personally through direct conversations; counsel papers the note or SAFEs so the funding is real debt or real equity, not an undocumented transfer.

parts.title: Draft the emergency cost plan: vendor cuts, founder salary, anything that moves the zero-cash date without touching owed wages

execution.rationale: Draft the cut scenarios from the books and the vendor ledger; management decides which cuts execute.

parts.title: Decide the fork while payroll can still be paid: bridge, cut to default-alive, or an orderly wind-down

execution.rationale: Founders and the board weigh the funded options and choose the path in a recorded decision; the choice spends other people's money and jobs.

parts.title: If the answer is wind down, start the shutdown while final wages can still be paid on time
parts.when: the fork decision is an orderly wind-down

execution.rationale: The wind-down decision and its first filings are founder and board acts under counsel; the referenced shutdown record carries the step-by-step mechanics.

parts.title: Tell the board before payday and the team before the rumor: board first, then managers, then everyone affected

execution.rationale: The founder delivers the news personally in sequence and answers questions; the message is the founder's own.

links.when: the fork decision is an orderly wind-down

metadata.trigger: The cash forecast says the next payroll will not clear: you are weeks from out of cash, or the provider's funding debit just failed.
metadata.supportReason: The deferral conversations, the bridge, and the fork decision are founder and counsel work; an agent can recompute the cash gap, tally the wage exposure, and draft the cost scenarios from the books.

contextNeeded.query: current cash, burn, and the payroll calendar with the provider's funding-debit date
